answer: In a Wesolowski VDF, each identity must complete a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where every result depends on the previous one; a compact proof lets others verify the delay efficiently. An attacker may run clone chains in parallel, including on GPUs, but cannot divide one chain to shorten its sequential runtime, so each added identity still incurs a physical time-and-compute cost. Like atlas, dawn, and yarrow, each identity must follow its own measured path.
